section_summary.extract_value: This section reports multi-group confirmatory factor analyses testing measurement invariance of the BAS-2 across Denmark, Portugal, and Sweden and across boys and girls. Results (reported in Table 4 and Supplementary Table 5) indicate evidence of metric and partial scalar invariance across the country pairs and metric and (partial) scalar invariance across sexes within the three countries.
section_summary.evidence_source: The results displayed in Table 4 and Supplementary Table 5 indicate that there was evidence of metric and partial scalar invariance across Denmark and Portugal (metric -CFI = .003, scalar -CFI = .024, and partial scalar -CFI = .008); Denmark and Sweden (metric -CFI = .001, scalar -CFI = .016, and partial scalar -CFI = .008); and Portugal and Sweden (metric -CFI = .004, scalar -CFI = .020, and partial scalar -CFI = .007). Next, multi-group CFAs on the girl and boy samples from each country were carried out in order to test whether the BAS-2 was invariant across sexes in the three languages. The results of the multi-group CFAs on BAS-2 showed that the BAS-2 is metric and partial scalar invariant across boys and girls in Denmark (metric -CFI = .003, scalar -CFI = .024, and partial scalar -CFI = .007) and metric and scalar invariant across boys and girls in Portugal (metric -CFI = .000, and scalar -CFI = .001) and Sweden (metric -CFI = .008, and scalar -CFI = .006; see Supplementary Table 5).
